question: What is the primary pathological hallmark of gout?

options.C: Destruction of articular cartilage by neutrophils
options.D: Infection of the synovial fluid by bacteria

explanation: Gout specifically develops when uric acid builds up and forms needle-like monosodium urate crystals inside the joints and soft tissues, triggering severe inflammation. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h1)

question: Which term describes the historic association of gout with wealthy lifestyles?
explanation: Historically, gout was termed the disease of kings because it disproportionately affected wealthy individuals who could afford rich foods and alcohol. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h1)

question: Which enzyme is primarily responsible for converting purine derivatives into uric acid?
explanation: Xanthine oxidase is the key metabolic enzyme that catalyses the final steps of purine degradation into uric acid. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h2)

question: Why does the presence of hyperuricemia alone not automatically confirm a diagnosis of gout?

options.A: Uric acid is completely insoluble and precipitates in every human body fluid
options.B: Many individuals with elevated serum urate never form tissue crystals or experience flares
options.C: Crystals only precipitate when white blood cell counts are severely depressed
options.D: Serum uric acid levels always drop to normal during an acute inflammatory attack

explanation: While hyperuricemia is a necessary precursor, many people live with high blood urate levels without ever developing symptomatic crystal deposition. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h2)

question: Which medication class is well known for increasing serum uric acid levels as a side effect?
explanation: Thiazide and loop diuretics reduce the renal excretion of uric acid, frequently precipitating hyperuricemia and gout flares in hypertensive patients. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h3)

question: What is the primary mechanism by which alcohol triggers acute gout attacks?

options.A: It directly dissolves existing tophi and releases thousands of crystals into the blood
options.B: It paralyzes the neutrophils, preventing them from clearing joint fluid
options.C: It increases purine synthesis while simultaneously impairing renal urate excretion
options.D: It binds directly to synovial membranes and alters cartilage pH

explanation: Alcohol metabolism accelerates purine breakdown into uric acid while dehydration and metabolic byproducts impair the kidneys' ability to filter it out. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h3)

question: What is the medical term for gout affecting the base of the big toe?
explanation: Podagra refers specifically to the acute inflammation and pain localized at the first metatarsophalangeal joint during a gout flare. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h4)

question: A patient presents to the emergency department reporting sudden, severe throbbing pain, intense redness, and swelling in the right big toe that woke them from sleep. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: The rapid onset, nocturnal presentation, extreme tenderness, and involvement of the first MTP joint are classic clinical hallmarks of an acute gout flare. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h4)

question: What are tophaceous deposits primarily composed of?

options.A: Calcium phosphate and degraded collagen matrix
options.B: Aggregates of monosodium urate crystals surrounded by inflammatory cells
options.C: Cholesterol plaques combined with necrotic fat cells
options.D: Infected purulent fluid walled off by fibrous connective tissue

explanation: Tophi are hard accumulations of sodium urate crystals accompanied by a chronic foreign-body giant cell inflammatory reaction. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h5)

question: What distinguishes intercritical gout from chronic tophaceous gout?

options.A: Intercritical gout always requires surgical intervention, whereas chronic gout is managed purely through diet
options.B: Intercritical gout has normal serum uric acid levels, while chronic gout always presents with hypouricemia
options.C: Intercritical gout features symptom-free periods between acute flares, whereas chronic tophaceous gout involves persistent joint damage and visible deposits
options.D: Intercritical gout only affects the kidneys, while chronic tophaceous gout is restricted to the big toe

explanation: The intercritical stage represents the quiet intervals between acute flares, whereas the advanced tophaceous stage involves persistent structural damage and nodular crystal deposits. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h5)

question: What optical feature do monosodium urate crystals display under polarized light microscopy?
explanation: Under polarized light, needle-shaped monosodium urate crystals show negative birefringence, appearing yellow when aligned parallel to the compensator and blue when perpendicular. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h6)

question: Why might a patient experiencing an acute gout flare have a normal serum uric acid level?

options.A: Uric acid completely disappears from the bloodstream once it enters the synovial space
options.B: Laboratory assays cannot measure uric acid accurately while joint inflammation is present
options.C: Renal clearance automatically doubles as soon as joint pain begins
options.D: Inflammatory cytokines and stress hormones during an acute attack can temporarily lower serum urate levels

explanation: Serum uric acid can be deceptively normal or even low during an acute flare due to increased urinary excretion driven by cortisol and inflammatory responses. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h6)

question: What is the primary mechanism of action of allopurinol in managing gout?

options.A: Inhibiting xanthine oxidase to reduce uric acid production
options.B: Suppressing neutrophil migration by binding to beta-tubulin
options.C: Neutralizing synovial pH to dissolve monosodium urate crystals
options.D: Blocking renal reabsorption of uric acid in the proximal tubule

explanation: Allopurinol works by blocking xanthine oxidase, the enzyme responsible for converting purines into uric acid, thereby lowering overall body urate burden. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h7)

question: Why is it clinically contraindicated to start urate-lowering therapy during an acute gout flare?

options.A: The liver cannot metabolize allopurinol while synovial inflammation is actively occurring
options.B: Renal blood flow drops to zero during a flare, preventing drug excretion
options.C: NSAIDs will chemically neutralize urate-lowering drugs if administered concurrently
options.D: Rapid changes in serum urate levels can destabilize existing crystals and worsen the acute inflammation

explanation: Initiating or altering urate-lowering medication during an acute attack causes abrupt shifts in serum urate, causing crystals to shed or partially dissolve and prolonging the flare. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h7)

question: A hospitalized patient with an acute gout flare in the left ankle expresses severe pain when the bedsheet touches the joint. What is the most appropriate nursing intervention?

options.A: Apply a warm, moist heating pad directly to the ankle continuously
options.B: Use a bed cradle to keep the linens elevated off the affected foot
options.C: Massage the joint gently to stimulate local circulation and relieve tension
options.D: Wrap the ankle tightly with a heavy elastic compression bandage

explanation: A bed cradle lifts the weight and pressure of bed linens off an exquisitely tender joint during an acute inflammatory flare. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h8)

question: What key message must a nurse convey to a patient newly prescribed allopurinol for chronic gout?

options.A: Double your dosage whenever you eat red meat or drink alcohol to counteract the purines
options.B: Take the pill only when you feel an acute twinge of pain starting in your big toe
options.C: Allopurinol should be stopped immediately if a mild headache or nausea develops on the first day
options.D: Medication must be taken daily on a long-term basis, even during pain-free intervals, to prevent future crystal buildup

explanation: Urate-lowering therapy requires consistent daily adherence to keep serum urate below saturation levels and gradually dissolve stored crystals. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h8)
